review_scope_note: Full-repository audit; the signing reviewer parsed analysis_n40.json directly and re-verified the headline statistics and the int64/int128 boundary argument.
verification_methods: Parsed analysis_n40.json: num_partitions = 37,338; max |chi| = 58,965,081,685,061,803,130,880 (~5.90e22, log10 = 22.77); char_table_time_seconds = 34,283.4 (= 9.52 h)
Checked the int64 boundary: 5.90e22 > 2^63 ~ 9.22e18 by a factor of ~6,400, so the stated need for int128 (or exact) accumulation in a full S_40 triple-sum is arithmetically correct
Verified p(40) = 37,338 against the standard partition function and the JSON's internal trends block (p(20) = 627, p(30) = 5,604 consistent)
Confirmed C(37340,3) = 8,676,344,691,980 for the unique-triple count quoted for a hypothetical full S_40 run

claim_reviews.claim: Complete S_40 character table computed: 37,338 partitions, ~9.5 h; max |chi| = 5.9e22.
claim_reviews.evidence: All three headline numbers match the committed analysis JSON exactly (37,338; 34,283.4 s; 58,965,081,685,061,803,130,880). p(40) = 37,338 is independently correct.
claim_reviews.concerns: The full character table itself lives on Hugging Face and was not re-downloaded for this audit; the committed analysis artifact is the verification basis.

claim_reviews.claim: A full S_40 Kronecker triple-sum requires int128 (or exact) GPU accumulation because max |chi| exceeds int64; therefore only targeted slices (hooks, near-rectangular, random samples) were computed.
claim_reviews.evidence: The overflow analysis is correct: 5.9e22 / 2^63 ~ 6.4e3, so even a single product chi^3/z_rho can overflow signed 64-bit. Declining to publish a full table rather than shipping overflow-corrupted numbers is precisely the right call — and worth noting as the counterpoint to the S_30 max-g defect flagged in the sibling review: here the boundary was respected.

sources.reference: Reviewer arithmetic; analysis_n40.json hook/near-rectangular/random-sample sections with timings

claim_reviews.claim: S_45 is infeasible at this architecture: 89,134 partitions imply a ~63 TB character table.
claim_reviews.evidence: p(45) = 89,134 is correct; 89,134^2 entries x 8 bytes = 63.6 TB confirms the estimate. Honest scoping of the frontier.

overall_assessment: Every checkable statistic on this page matches the committed analysis artifact exactly, and the two boundary arguments (int64 overflow at 5.9e22; 63 TB at S_45) are arithmetically correct. The page's defining virtue is restraint: it explicitly refuses to publish a full triple-sum that its own overflow analysis shows would be unsound at int64. That is the discipline computational mathematics requires.
recommendations: When the int128 kernel lands, seed it with the S_30 dimension-bound invariant recommended in the S_30 review
certification_justification: Headline numbers verified against committed artifacts; boundary arithmetic independently confirmed; scope honestly limited by a correct overflow analysis.
